fitAnalysis.assessment:
Your 48% match is a weak fit for this Senior FP&A Analyst role, so upskilling is recommended first.

**Strengths:**
- Five years of forecasting, budgeting and variance analysis experience
- Month-end reporting and freight invoice reconciliations
- Power BI dashboards built on SAP data

**Gaps:**
- No cloud or AI vendor spend experience
- No accruals, allocations or cloud billing data analysis
- No FinOps or cloud cost management background

**Recommendation:** Build hands-on exposure to cloud billing data and FinOps (for example, a certification and a personal cost-analysis project) and target mid-level FP&A roles first, then reapply at senior level.

coverLetter:
Tomas Brandt
Chicago, IL, USA
tomas.brandt@example.com
+1 555 0123

October 12, 2026

Hiring Manager
GitLab

Dear Hiring Manager,

Your Cloud Hosting team needs forecasts that keep pace with changing usage and business drivers, and a forecast is only useful if people trust it. At Calder Industrial Components, the larger of my two business units was running at 88% forecast accuracy. I rebuilt the model around order backlog and brought it to 96%.

As a Financial Analyst, I own the monthly forecast and variance reporting for two business units, so the month-end close activities and variance analysis in your ad are daily work for me. I also shortened our close reporting from 9 working days to 6 by automating journal checks in Excel VBA, and I build Power BI dashboards on SAP data that plant managers use. I haven't worked with cloud or AI vendor spend, so I'd be learning provider billing exports from scratch. My five years in budgeting, forecasting and month-end reporting, plus advanced Excel and basic SQL, give me a solid base for that, and I'm working towards my ACCA qualification (9 of 13 papers passed).

Working asynchronously with engineering and finance leaders suits how I like to work: own the deliverable, flag risks early and explain the numbers clearly. I'm available to talk whenever suits your team, and I'd welcome the chance to walk you through how I rebuilt that forecast model.

Best regards,
Tomas Brandt
